newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal mixed, soyoil lower on planting ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal mixed, soyoil lower on planting ideas.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures were mixed with nearby months down and soyoil futures were lower amid speculation U.S. farmers would plow up damaged soft red winter wheat and plant more soybeans, traders said.
Traders speculated eastern Corn Belt farmers would replant flood-damaged wheat acreage to soybeans, especially with new crop soybean values at a lofty $7.35-1/2 per bushel.

Meanwhile, soy product exports were expected to taper off after soymeal prices hit 8-1/2 year highs Monday, pricing some buyers out of the market. USDA said Brazil would fill the void with soybean exports expected to jump to 5.2 million tonnes.

Traders also cited news the Philippines was considering buying South American soymeal instead of U.S. supplies due to high prices. Philippine soymeal imports were expected to climb to 1.4 million tonnes this year, from 1.2 million last year.

But talk that several major U.S. crushers were taking down time this month was considered supportive and crushing rates were expected to drop this week. Cargill Inc said it's Guntersville crusher will be down for about two weeks and others may shut temporarily as well, sources said.
At 1114 CST, soymeal was $1.70 a ton lower to $0.80 higher with May down $0.60 at $273.20.
Soyoil was off 0.30 to 0.20 cent per lb with May off 0.29 at 25.88.
Commercials were on both sides of the soyoil market with ADM reportedly a seller of 400 lots August and 200 lots each July and December. But Cargill Inc bought 800 lots May soyoil, traders said.
Refco Inc sold 500 lots May soyoil and O'Connor and Co sold 300 lots May, traders said.
